title: time-aware-embedding-autoscaler-and-tenant-surge-smoothing
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description: Build and deploy a time-aware autoscaler and tenant surge-smoothing layer for the embeddings endpoint to improve p95/p99 latency under bursts while reducing cost from unnecessary GPU allocations. This ticket covers design, implementation, and rollout of: (1) a short-term demand predictor (15–120s horizon) feeding autoscaler decisions, (2) a reservoir-based surge buffer that smooths transient spikes without immediate scaling, (3) deterministic tenant admission control (leaky/token-bucket hybrid) to protect p99 SLOs, and (4) warm-pool and KV-cache prewarming heuristics for fast scale-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler reduces unnecessary scale-ups by >= 30% on historical burst traces while keeping p99 latency delta <= +10% compared to baseline
Tenant admission control enforces tenant-level fair-share and prevents single tenant from causing p99 violations for others in 95% of simulated bursts
Warm-pool preheat reduces cold-start token latency by >= 40% in synthetic scale-up tests
Operational metrics (scale decisions, queue length, predicted demand, reservoir occupancy) are emitted to Console and dashboards with <60s freshness
Canary rollout is possible per-region and per-tier with automatic rollback on SLO breach
design_notes: Predictor: lightweight exponential smoothing + short window AR predictor running in scaler service (15s sampling, 60s lookback). Conservatively bias predictions upward by configurable headroom factor (default 1.15).

Reservoir: time-decayed token reservoir sized by worker concurrency and median token-per-request to absorb short bursts; reservoir drains first and triggers scale only when occupancy > threshold for N consecutive samples.

Admission: hybrid per-tenant leaky bucket with priority queues: realtime tenants get higher refill, background tenants rate-limited. Admission returns detailed reject codes so clients can implement retry/backoff.
Warm-pool: maintain small pool of idle workers with warmed KV cache mapping for hot models; use predictive eviction based on usage frequency and model size.
Metrics: new metrics: embeddings_predicted_qps, embeddings_reservoir_occupancy, tenant_backpressure_rate, warm_pool_fill_ratio, scale_decision_reason. Tag by model_id, region, and tenant_id.
Cost model: track GPU-minutes saved vs extra reservoir memory and cold-warm pool overhead; aim for net cost-neutral or savings for long-tail burst workloads.
progress_updates: 2026-02-06: Kickoff meeting with infra, serving-runtime, and observability teams. Agreed on predictor approach and reservoir concept.
2026-02-09: Prototype predictor implemented in Python and validated against 7 days of production traces; MAPE ~18% on 60s horizon when using 1.15 headroom.
2026-02-12: Admission control design reviewed by Security and Product; request to include observability tags for tenant_id hashed to 64-bit for PII compliance.
2026-02-15: Warm-pool prototype integrated with runtime warm-start API. KV-cache snapshotting API stabilized.
2026-02-18: Load tests in staging show reservoir reduces scale-ups by 37% on synthetic burst workload but increased average queue length by 12% (within target). Preparing canary plan.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Predictor underestimates sustained ramps -> could delay necessary scaling. Mitigation: default conservative headroom and fallback to queue-length-triggered immediate scale-up.
Risk: Reservoir or admission control could increase tail latency for high-priority tenants. Mitigation: priority queues with strict cutoff and emergency bypass for critical SLOs.
Risk: Warm-pool memory footprint on GPUs -> might reduce overall capacity. Mitigation: cap warm pool size per region and evict cold entries by LRU with size-aware policy.
Risk: Incorrect tenant tagging could leak identifiers. Mitigation: hash tenant_id before emitting metrics and review with Security for compliance.
testing_plan: Unit tests for predictor logic and headroom application
End-to-end staging runs replaying 14 days of production ingestion traces with A/B: baseline vs reservoir+predictor
Chaos test: simulate worker failures during scale-up to validate graceful degradation and fallback to higher-latency model-variants
Canary rollout: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% with SLO monitoring and automated rollback on sustained p99 breach
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal): deploy to staging and run 48h soak with synthetic bursts
Phase B (canary): enable for <1% production traffic in us-west with tight SLO alarms
Phase C (regional ramp): expand to other regions and tenant tiers after 72h stable metrics
Phase D (full): flip default and monitor cost/latency delta for 2 weeks before declaring Done
notes_for_reviewers: Please review predictor headroom and reservoir sizing equations in the design doc; numbers are intentionally conservative for first rollout.
Security: verify hashing scheme for tenant_id metrics and approve telemetry schema change before canary.
SRE: are the proposed alerts and runbook steps sufficient for automatic rollback?
